sections.title: The letter ó
paragraphs: The letter name is (ó) /oː/. Its main sound is a vowel, heard in (óra) /ˈoː.rɒ/, which means clock, hour. A vowel is a sound made with open air and no touch in the mouth. This letter always has one sound.

sections.title: Saying the sound
paragraphs: Pull your tongue back into the middle of your mouth. Make your lips into a tight circle. Turn your voice on and let the air flow smoothly. This sound is long, so hold it for more time. Touch your throat with your hand to feel the strong shake.

sections.title: Reading the letter
paragraphs: The accent mark tells you that this vowel is long. An accent mark is a diacritic written above a letter. This letter makes its long sound in all positions. You hear it at the start of a word in (óra) /ˈoː.rɒ/. You also hear it at the end of a word in (só) /ʃoː/.

sections.title: Tips for English speakers
paragraphs: Do not let this sound glide into two pieces like the vowel in boat. That English sound is a diphthong. A diphthong is two vowel sounds in one syllable, where the sound glides from the first to the second. Keep your lips and tongue completely still until you finish speaking.
